overall_summary: Recent 7-day performance metrics clearly show that extreme space and astrophysics content—specifically hypothetical 'What If' scenarios and bizarre planetary properties—outperforms standard biological or historical facts by a significant margin in views-per-day and engagement (likes-per-view). Topics featuring extreme environments (diamonds, extreme darkness, unusual rain types) dominate the top tier of recent traction.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) generated over 950-1,000+ views rapidly with high like ratios (38 likes).
winning_patterns.action: Double down on visually striking 'What If' scenarios involving extreme cosmic entities or unusual planetary surfaces.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) rapidly accumulated ~1,000 views and strong engagement within days of release.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form spotlights on lesser-known, extreme exoplanets with mind-bending physical properties.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on songs stuck in the head (ef3ND4qiRHc, Jc04LVKNd2s) or basic memory tricks stalled out below 100 views with minimal engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological facts and brain tricks unless framed within a high-stakes or mystery narrative.

weak_patterns.pattern: Low-Impact Animal Facts without Extreme Stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: Standard animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (AXAfwrzzEdU) had modest lifetime views but plateaued heavily in daily velocity compared to space content.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal content away from static trivia toward cinematic animal survival or extreme prehistoric comparisons.
